trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards; going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down.
Going right would leave both cell (4,6) and number 3 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Going left would strand number 3: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going down, the next 12 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,3). So the line goes left.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Going down, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4). So the line goes right.
Going down, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,3). So the line goes right.
The line must go right: down is number 10, which comes later.
Going down would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes left.
Going up would wall in number 10, the last number; going left would cut off the left side (3 cells). So the line goes down.
Going down would cut off the bottom edge (4 cells). So the line goes right.
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
